finding.title: History inspection bundles saved-state safety and dirty-editor preservation
finding.public_requirement: task/environment/instructions/behaviour.md:34 separately names current saved version and unsaved draft; both are promised to remain unchanged during older-revision inspection.
finding.criterion: task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:507-512 cw_history_inspection_draft is one binary outcome of weight 0.6 requiring both the actual dirty draft and current saved record unchanged.
finding.procedure: task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:467 obtains both an actual dirty-editor observation and a fresh current-record observation, then assigns both to history_inspection_draft.
finding.why_not_setup: The pre-inspection dirty draft and accepted current head establish setup. Their respective after-inspection preservation results are two separate protection promises. A server readback here does not establish that the client draft survived, and a preserved draft does not establish that the server head stayed unchanged.

counterexamples.implementation: A read-only history endpoint/view never writes the saved head, but closing inspection replaces the three unsaved editor fields with the saved head.
counterexamples.lost_observed_outcome: Valid persisted-state protection gets no independent credit.

counterexamples.implementation: The history dialog snapshots and restores all dirty editor fields, but its inspect action mistakenly calls the restore endpoint and changes the saved head.
counterexamples.lost_observed_outcome: Valid dirty-editor preservation gets no independent credit.

finding.fix: Retain the one S37 step-2 shared scenario and split its two already-collected observations into separate binary outcomes with the same combined 0.6 weight; continue the draft observation even if the fresh saved read is wrong, and vice versa.
finding.score_bound: The current 0.6-weight conjunction carries 0.6 / 45.25 of Functional, or approximately 0.007956 of total shaped reward above the existing gate/floor. This is a bounded partial-credit defect, not an empirical score claim.

adversarial_checks_without_additional_fi: A stopped preview that suppresses old handlers but removes content can retain cw_completed_stop while failing cw_completed_stop_preview; separate observations and fallback controls are explicit (Functional prompt:148-160).

A stale Save refused by the server while the real dirty editor loses fields can retain server-refusal credit; draft preservation and subsequent reapply are separately owned (Functional prompt:440-445).
Current-record restart survival, history restart survival, remembered retry survival and post-restart writing have distinct owners and fallback paths (Functional prompt:430-434).

History snapshots created by ordinary Saves, snapshots retained through deliberate restore, browser-reload durability, and process-restart durability are different transitions. Reusing the records does not duplicate one observation.
Matching controls, cancellation markers and fresh reads necessary to establish one negative/atomic outcome are valid setup/readback, not automatically separate promises.

A conforming alternative can use a read-only dialog or side panel, retain the dirty buffer separately, use non-unit revision advances, automatically retry a lost restore reply, and use static rollback pictures. The prompts explicitly permit these; no incompatible-product demand was established.
Visual desktop geometry versus font choices and mobile usability versus responsive composition have explicit non-duplication ownership (Visual prompt:17-29 and Visual judge:99).
limits: No other reviewer report or historical verdict was consulted. All 141 recorded frozen-source/policy/index-artifact hashes matched.
